column3: Close to the Hebrew; “To graze” is rendered “To pasture his flock,” and “spice” as “balsam.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Grazing” is rendered “pastures his flock.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Majestic like the hosts with banners” is rendered “As awesome as an army with banners,” and “friend” as “darling.”
Close to the Hebrew; “She-goats” is rendered “goats.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Young women” is rendered “maidens.”
Close to the Hebrew; “One is she” is rendered “is unique,” “daughters” as “The maidens,” and NASB adds “But” and “saying.”
“The one who looks down like the dawn” is rendered “that grows like the dawn,” and “majestic like the hosts with banners” as “As awesome as an army with banners.”
Close to the Hebrew; “A garden of nut” is rendered “the orchard of nut trees,” “green shoots” as “blossoms,” and “the wadi” as “the valley.”
The Hebrew is obscure (“I did not know, my desire set me [on] the chariots of my people, a prince”); NASB renders “my soul set me Over the chariots of my noble people.” The meaning is uncertain.
MT 7:1. NASB divides the verse between speakers; “return” is rendered “Come back,” and “like the dance of the two groups” as “As at the dance of the two companies.”
